title: Israeli Fire Kills Three in Gaza — Rimal Drone Strike and Beit Lahia 'Yellow Line' Shooting
detail: On Thursday, September 3, 2026, Israeli fire killed at least three Palestinians in Gaza in two separate incidents. In the Rimal neighborhood of western Gaza City, an Israeli combat drone fired at least two missiles at a group of civilians near the Near East Council of Churches building on Ath-Thawara Street, killing one person and wounding several others. Separately, in Beit Lahia in northern Gaza, Israeli forces opened fire on a group of Palestinians, killing two; the IDF said in a statement it had 'eliminated two terrorists who crossed the Yellow Line' — the buffer zone separating IDF-occupied parts of Gaza from the rest of the enclave — but offered no evidence the men were armed. Gaza health officials said the strikes brought the toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to more than 1,330 Palestinians killed, against roughly four Israeli soldiers over the same period.

confidenceReason: Rimal strike confirmed by WAFA's own reporting citing witnesses; Beit Lahia shooting confirmed by the IDF's own statement, which named the 'Yellow Line' justification but provided no evidence the victims were armed; Al Jazeera corroborates both incidents and the cumulative post-ceasefire toll.

title: Ben Gvir Unveils 'Disengagement 710' Plan to Relocate 1.86 Million Palestinians From Gaza
detail: On Thursday, September 3, 2026, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir unveiled a party platform he called 'Disengagement 710' — a reference to Israel's 2005 Gaza withdrawal and the October 7, 2023 attack — proposing what he termed the 'voluntary emigration' of most of Gaza's roughly 2.3 million Palestinians ahead of the October 27 Israeli election. The plan targets 250,000 departures within the first year, 1.11 million within three years, and 1.86 million within seven years, to be administered by a newly created government ministry offering emigrants travel assistance, initial housing, vocational training, and up to 24 months of financial support. Proposed destination countries include Turkey, Ethiopia, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and unspecified Arab states, none of which have agreed to accept Gazans. Ben Gvir's Otzma Yehudit party estimated an initial NIS 10 billion ($3 billion) Israeli investment, with up to NIS 50 billion ($15.2 billion) more contingent on international matching funds. 'Instead of illusions of peace now, we need actions of emigration now,' Ben Gvir said. 'Instead of [Gazans] digging tunnels, it's time to pack suitcases.' Legal analysts note that forced or coerced civilian displacement from occupied territory constitutes a war crime under the Geneva Conventions; the plan was widely described as facing steep international opposition and unlikely to be implemented.

media.caption: National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir unveils the 'Disengagement 710' Gaza emigration plan, September 3, 2026

confidenceReason: The plan and its terms are drawn directly from Ben Gvir's own platform announcement, corroborated by Times of Israel, Al Jazeera and Jerusalem Post reporting; the 'voluntary' characterization and feasibility are Ben Gvir's own framing and are independently disputed by international law analysts cited in the same reports.

title: Police Arrest Four More Suspects, Including IDF Conscript, in Settler Violence Crackdown
detail: On Thursday, September 3, 2026, Israeli police announced the arrest of four more suspects in connection with Jewish extremist violence against Palestinians in the West Bank. Two settlers were detained at Ben Gurion Airport as they attempted to depart for Uman, Ukraine, ahead of the Hasidic pilgrimage there for Rosh Hashanah; one is an IDF conscript arrested in cooperation with military police over suspected involvement in settler-violence incidents. A 29-year-old settler was separately arrested in northern Israel after repeatedly violating a court-ordered decree requiring him to report daily to a police station. The arrests follow a 19-year-old settler's earlier arrest over the August 29 Qusra home-takeover siege, though police said the wider group of settlers involved in that incident remained in the village with no further arrests made.

media.caption: Israeli police announce four more arrests in the settler-violence crackdown, September 3, 2026
